reason: E1 directly supports the formation of a Pt-rich shell and M–N bonds via acid-etching and thermal annealing in a similar HEA system, and links this to enhanced durability. However, the cited evidence is entirely from electrocatalysis under electrochemical conditions, not automotive exhaust catalysis with H2O and NO, so the premise of effectiveness under the specified exhaust conditions is unsupported. E2 and E3 are irrelevant to the proposed treatment or mechanism.
premises: Acid-etching selectively leaches less noble metals from a multi-element alloy, driving Pt surface segregation.
A low-temperature nitrogen anneal incorporates nitrogen and forms stabilizing M–N bonds in the treated alloy.
The combined treatment creates a Pt-rich shell on an intact high-entropy alloy core.
This core–shell structure with M–N bonds enhances catalytic durability and activity retention.
The treatment is effective under transient, low-temperature exhaust conditions with H2O and NO.
